headline: High: n8n’s writable, broad-egress workflow engine can turn Great Expectations outputs into unsafe downstream actions; prompt-injection and leakage are lower but present via shared files.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Great Expectations reads and writes files for data sources, validation results, and documentation, while n8n can read/write the server filesystem and pass workflow node outputs between steps. That creates a plausible file-based instruction bridge if n8n ingests Great Expectations artifacts as trusted content. No direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF n8n workflows parse Great Expectations-generated files as instructions or prompts
IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory without content provenance checks
mitigations: Store Great Expectations outputs in a read-only directory for n8n
Add a filename allowlist before n8n reads validation artifacts
Prefix all machine-generated files with an untrusted-data marker
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to workflow inputs
requires-engineering: isolate the two agents into separate workspaces

B_data_leakage.rationale: Great Expectations touches validation results and documentation, and n8n has broad network egress plus access to per-credential secrets and workflow-processed data. If n8n reads Great Expectations files from the shared server filesystem, sensitive validation outputs can be forwarded to third-party integrations. The pair is open-source, but the documented filesystem and egress surfaces make leakage plausible in default deployments.
conditions: IF Great Expectations validation results contain sensitive data classes
IF n8n workflows send those files or extracted fields to an external integration node
mitigations: Restrict n8n workflows from reading Great Expectations output directories
Mask sensitive columns before validation artifacts are written
Disable unused outbound integration nodes
Rotate and scope n8n credentials to the minimum workflow
requires-engineering: enforce DLP checks on workflow inputs and outputs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Great Expectations can install packages and write validation artifacts, while n8n can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, and write the filesystem. Even though n8n does not modify git state, both agents can mutate the same server files if co-located, creating write contention and accidental overwrites. The shared-state model in n8n increases the likelihood of conflicts.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory or project checkout
IF n8n shell steps write files that Great Expectations also updates
mitigations: Separate output directories per agent
Use a lock file around shared writes
Run Great Expectations in read-only mode for shared inputs
Avoid shell steps that mutate the same workspace
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: n8n is an orchestration engine with tool-calling workflow nodes, so it can treat Great Expectations outputs as authoritative inputs and then act on them. Great Expectations produces validation results and documentation, but no verification boundary is documented between the two agents. That makes a bad validation artifact capable of cascading into downstream automated actions, which is dangerous by default.
conditions: IF n8n workflows branch or trigger actions from Great Expectations validation results
IF those results are consumed without an explicit human verification step
mitigations: Insert a manual approval step before any action node
Require schema validation on Great Expectations outputs
Log and diff validation artifacts before execution
Limit n8n to read-only reporting workflows
requires-engineering: add signed attestations for validation results

E_compliance.rationale: Great Expectations is a data-quality tool with documentation and validation-result handling, while n8n processes whatever the workflow touches and stores credentials on its server. If regulated data flows through n8n workflows, retention and residency controls can diverge from the source system’s expectations. The profiles do not prove a specific residency breach, so this stays medium.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through n8n workflows
IF n8n retention or credential storage exceeds the source system’s policy
mitigations: Review n8n retention settings before enabling regulated workflows
Avoid storing regulated payloads in workflow history
Scope credentials to the minimum necessary integrations
Document data residency for each connected node
requires-engineering: implement policy checks on workflow creation
